Utility Mark-Out Before Every Solon Grind

Because a stump grinder works below grade, an underground utility mark-out through the Ohio Utilities Protection Service (OUPS / 811) is required before the wheel touches the stump. Roubic schedules that mark-out at booking as part of the job — there is no separate homeowner filing to chase down and no waiting on your end.

On tight-access residential lots we bring the compact 36-inch-gate grinder; larger corridors and commercial parcels get the full-size track grinder. Access, soil, and structure proximity are all confirmed on the free on-site walk.

What Happens If You Wait

The Cost of Leaving a Stump — Solon Context

Three reasons a leftover stump gets more expensive, not less, the longer it sits.

Regrowth & Suckering

Many hardwood stumps push up suckers and root sprouts for years. Left alone, a single stump can send shoots across a Solon lawn and back into beds you just planted.

Pest & Decay Harborage

A decaying stump becomes a nest for carpenter ants, termites, and wood-decay fungi that can migrate to healthy trees and structures nearby. Grinding removes the food source.

Trip Hazard & Mower Damage

A hidden stump is a liability for guests and a wrecked mower blade waiting to happen. On commercial Solon parcels it is also a documented walkway hazard.

Common Solon Grinding Questions

Solon Stump Grinding FAQ

Six things Solon homeowners want to know before booking.

How much does stump grinding cost in Solon?
Solon stump grinding starts at a $150 minimum per visit. Most single residential stumps (12–30" DBH) run $200–$450. Heritage 60"+ stumps that need the full-size track grinder run $450–$900+. Multiple stumps at the same address get a per-stump volume rate, and grinding paired with a Roubic removal qualifies for a package discount.
Will Roubic grind a stump from a tree another company removed?
Yes — we routinely grind stumps left by other contractors, storm-fallen trees the homeowner cleared, and stumps inherited with a property purchase. Booking is the same as any other grinding job, and the standard $150 minimum applies.
How deep does Roubic grind stumps in Solon?
Our standard grind takes the stump 6–12 inches below grade — deep enough to plant grass, lay sod, install pavers, or pour a small pad over. We can grind deeper on request if you're planning new construction or a replant in the same hole.
Do you handle chip cleanup after grinding?
Yes — full chip cleanup is the default. Optional backfill with topsoil is available for an additional fee if you want the hole filled and ready for seed. If you'd rather keep the chips as mulch elsewhere on your property, we'll leave them at no charge.
Do I need to arrange an underground utility mark-out first?
No — because a grinder works below grade, an OUPS / 811 utility mark-out is required, and Roubic schedules it for you at booking. There's no homeowner filing to chase down and no waiting on your end; we confirm the marks are in before the crew grinds.
Is Roubic licensed and insured for stump grinding in Solon?
Yes — Roubic Tree & Landscape LLC carries full general liability and workers-compensation coverage, with certificates of insurance provided on request before any work begins. The company is family-owned and has carried continuous coverage since 1982, with a 5.0 rating across Google reviews.
